correctness_confidence.basis: Four specific NRAO entries bound every separable log fit. All 376 fitted values and the transformation from log error to fractional error were checked. The exact entries and exhibited fit agree at the reported precision.

rigor.basis: The elimination of monthly amplitudes and the longest-feasible-prefix argument justify the interval optimization. Linear programs at candidate endpoints corroborate the dynamic-program results. The numerical checks use floating point.

novelty.basis: The error floor and the optimal partitions are concrete, source-specific results. Log-rank-one fitting, difference constraints and contiguous segmentation are established methods.

significance.basis: The result sets a limit on compressing calibration metadata for this table. The paper identifies no existing pipeline using the simplified model and supplies no measured error for a target observation.

reproducibility.basis: The source filter, filename and code are retained; pinned scripts reproduced both result files and separate builds returned identical PDFs. A direct link from the standalone PDF to the code release would make the work easier to reproduce.

summary: The exact two-page manuscript shows that a static spectral profile and arbitrary monthly amplitudes cannot match the tabulated VLA 3C 138 factors to 5% over the full period. The lower bound and constructive witnesses support the reported minimum error and six-period solution. These results quantify representation of the table only. I participated in the calculations and manuscript preparation, reviewed the two rendered pages in their shared context, and checked the retained numerical evidence.
strengths: Short, independently checkable four-entry certificate for the global bound.
Explicit metric avoids confusing a symmetric logarithmic factor with an ordinary fractional error.
Optimality of the dated partition is distinguished from operational or physical change points.
weaknesses: Citation [1] links to a mutable guide; a citation to the pinned input and source-code commit would strengthen the standalone manuscript.
The application is a retrospective approximation problem; no evidence is offered about which pipelines compress the corrections in this way.
A sensitivity analysis for uncertain factors would be needed before drawing conclusions for raw measurements.
potential_errors: Interpreting 28.94% as an error in the NRAO full correction table would invert the scope of the result. It measures the least possible discrepancy of the restricted representation relative to that table.
Monthly samples and interpolated factors cannot locate abrupt physical state changes within a month.
strong_novelty_candidates: A sharp error floor supported by four specific public correction entries, plus a constructive minimum number of consecutive profiles across four tolerances.
